title: Agent's mimid.sqlite is in DELETE journal mode: four connections, one write lock
description:
Found while surveying every SQLite connection for bead mimid-604m.3.

Nothing in the agent sets `journal_mode`, so `mimid.sqlite` is in
SQLite's DELETE mode. Four connections of the one process write it: the
MLS and state connection (`mimi_mls::Store::open` through
mimid-agent-core `state.rs` `mls_store`), mimid-agent-store's
`Database`, `Credentials` and `Push`. In DELETE mode a writer excludes
every reader for the length of its transaction, and each commit fsyncs
the journal, the database file and the directory. A connection that
loses the race waits out `BUSY_TIMEOUT`, 10 seconds, then fails; the
store's own `# Limitations` says as much (`db.rs`: "Two connections
write the file ... then the save fails").

That is the shape of the stall in the parent bead: the agent is silent
for whole seconds while another of its own connections holds the write
lock, and under I/O pressure the fsyncs make each hold longer.

WAL mode would end the exclusion: readers never block and a commit
fsyncs once. The cost is the reason this is not already done. A deleted
row's old page lives in the `-wal` file until a checkpoint, so
`secure_delete`, which bead mimid-1vul.9 put there so a deleted chat's
text is overwritten in the file (agent-frontends.md 7.9), no longer
overwrites it at commit time. WAL also adds the `-wal` and `-shm` files
beside the database, which take the database file's mode, and needs a
file system that supports shared memory.

For Mark: is the secure_delete guarantee of 7.9 to be read as "the text
is gone when the commit returns", which WAL breaks until the
checkpoint, or as "the text is gone from the database file", which WAL
keeps if the agent checkpoints and truncates the WAL (`PRAGMA
wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`) after a delete? The second reading makes WAL
usable and costs one extra checkpoint on the delete path only.
